dropped.finding: The new probe summary `[rebar probe - safe to delete] ...` is passed unescaped into the `summary ~ "{summary}"` fallback search. Jira's text search treats `[`, `]` and `-` as reserved characters. The square brackets parse as a range query, which will likely be rejected as invalid (HTTP 400). The ` - safe` part can parse as NOT `safe`, which would exclude the issue even when the query is accepted. Either way the summary fallback can no longer find the probe issue, so the poll now depends only on the key search. The fake-client tests cannot catch this because they ignore the JQL.
scenarios: Live probe run: every summary fallback search returns HTTP 400 (invalid text query) or finds nothing, so each attempt line shows `summary: error HTTP 400` and only the key search can ever detect visibility
dropped.suggested_fix: Pass a plain, reserved-character-free search term into the summary fallback, e.g. `_poll_until_visible(client, key, f"{DELETE_ME_MARKER} delete-permission probe", attempts=attempts)`, instead of `payload["title"]`. Alternatively, escape `[]-` etc. with `\\` inside the JQL string.

dropped.finding: No offline test runs the summary search with the probe's real summary. The diff adds a summary prefix with reserved Lucene/JQL characters (`[`, `]`, ` - `), and it goes unescaped into `summary ~ "{summary}"`. Every new poll test passes the placeholder "synthetic summary" to fake clients that ignore the JQL. If Jira rejects that query, or the brackets and hyphen are read as query operators, nothing offline catches it. The fallback search would quietly stop working and only show up as error notes in a live failure.
scenarios: The live probe's key search lags, and the summary fallback is sent `summary ~ "[rebar probe - safe to delete] DELETE-ME-d01e delete-permission probe"`. Jira rejects it or matches nothing, so the fallback is silently gone while every offline test stays green.
